desc:
The strings s and t have the same length and contain exactly the same letters with the same multiplicities (t is an anagram of s). In one move you may swap two neighbouring characters of s.

Return the minimum number of moves needed to turn s into t.

s = "abc", t = "cba"   result = 3
s = "aabb", t = "bbaa" result = 4
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters
t is a rearrangement of s
hints: If all letters were different, the target would tell you where each letter of s must go. What do you do when letters repeat?

Equal letters never need to cross each other, so the k-th occurrence of a letter in s should become the k-th occurrence of that letter in t. This turns the task into sorting a permutation by adjacent swaps.
The minimum number of adjacent swaps to sort a permutation is its number of inversions. Build the permutation from t and count inversions in O(n log n) with a Fenwick tree (or merge sort).
editorial: Match equal letters in order: the k-th c of t is paired with the k-th c of s. Crossing two equal letters is wasted effort, so this matching is optimal. Let pos[i] be the index in s of the letter matched with t[i]; this is a permutation of 0..n-1.

Turning s into t now means sorting pos by adjacent swaps, since each adjacent swap fixes at most one inversion, and bubble sort fixes exactly one per swap. So the answer is the number of inversions of pos. Count them with a Fenwick tree: scan pos left to right and, for each value, add the number of already seen values that are larger. Time O(n log n), space O(n). The answer can reach n(n-1)/2 ≈ 2 × 108, which fits in 32 bits.
solution:
from collections import defaultdict, deque


def minAdjacentSwaps(s, t):
    n = len(s)
    where = defaultdict(deque)
    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
        where[ch].append(i)
    pos = [where[ch].popleft() for ch in t]
    tree = [0] * (n + 1)
    inv = 0
    for seen, p in enumerate(pos):
        # count earlier values <= p, the rest are larger than p
        i = p + 1
        smaller = 0
        while i > 0:
            smaller += tree[i]
            i -= i & -i
        inv += seen - smaller
        i = p + 1
        while i <= n:
            tree[i] += 1
            i += i & -i
    return inv
